outcomes.text: {name} waved the trailer onto a bridge that was lower than the map said. The stage arrived with a dent and spent a month being checked.

outcomes.headline: The drivers' job
outcomes.text: The stage travels with the transport crew.

decisions.headline: Who writes the assembly procedures?
decisions.text: The technicians are working from marked-up drawings and memory. The quality office wants a proper step-by-step procedure for the whole assembly, written by someone who understands the hardware.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the procedure.

outcomes.headline: {name}'s little book
outcomes.text: {name} spent a month on the workshop floor and wrote a procedure the technicians actually like. Mistakes in assembly drop sharply.

outcomes.headline: Written from a desk
outcomes.text: {name} wrote it from the drawings without asking the technicians. Half the steps are in the wrong order, and they ignore it.

options.label: The technicians know what they're doing

outcomes.headline: From memory
outcomes.text: The assembly goes on as before.

decisions.headline: Who checks the wiring?
decisions.text: The craft has thousands of wires, and the drawings and the hardware no longer quite agree. Someone has to trace every connection against the drawings before the panels are closed for good.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the more mistakes are caught.

outcomes.headline: {name} found two crossed wires
outcomes.text: {name} traced every wire with a meter and a highlighter. Two were swapped at a connector: in flight, a command would have done the opposite of what it said.

outcomes.headline: {name} bent a pin
outcomes.text: {name} probed too hard and bent a connector pin. It took a week to find why the craft wouldn't power up.

options.label: Just power it up and see
options.shows: Sure to give about half a season's gain.

outcomes.headline: It powered up
outcomes.text: Everything that was tested worked. The wiring that wasn't tested is anyone's guess.

decisions.headline: Who goes to the wind tunnel?
decisions.text: The team has three days in a borrowed wind tunnel, and more questions than time. Someone has to decide on the spot which runs to make, and in what order.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the more the three days answer.

outcomes.headline: {name} got the most out of it
outcomes.text: {name} dropped the safe runs and went straight for the doubtful ones. Three days answered a season's worth of questions.

outcomes.headline: {name} ran out of time
outcomes.text: {name} spent two days on runs that confirmed what everyone knew, and the important ones never happened.

options.label: Send the tunnel staff a list
options.shows: Sure to give about half a season's gain.

outcomes.headline: By the list
outcomes.text: The tunnel staff work through the list in order and post the results.

decisions.headline: Who trains the new technicians?
decisions.text: Six new technicians start next week, straight from trade school. Someone experienced has to teach them the hardware before they're let near it.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the new hands will be.

options.label: Put an engineer in charge of them

outcomes.headline: {name}'s class of six
outcomes.text: {name} ran the six through every job twice. Within a month they're as careful as the old hands, and {name} enjoyed it more than expected.

outcomes.headline: Bad habits, taught well
outcomes.text: {name} taught them fast and taught them shortcuts. Small faults start turning up in their work.

outcomes.headline: Learning by doing
outcomes.text: The new technicians learn by watching the others.

decisions.headline: Who signs the acceptance tests?
decisions.text: The craft is about to go through the tests that decide whether it's fit to fly. Someone has to sign each one off, and refuse to sign when it isn't right, whatever the schedule says.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the chance a fault is caught before flight.

outcomes.headline: {name} refused to sign
outcomes.text: {name} wouldn't sign one test with a reading at the edge of its limit. The part behind it was failing slowly. It's replaced.

outcomes.headline: {name} signed under pressure
outcomes.text: With the schedule pressing, {name} signed a marginal reading. The part failed in a later test, and the craft lost weeks.

options.label: The team lead signs as usual

outcomes.headline: Signed as usual
outcomes.text: The team lead signs each test as it passes.

decisions.headline: Who decides what can be saved?
decisions.text: A fire in a test cell scorched a test unit. Some of its parts might be reused; others may be weakened in ways that don't show. Someone has to decide what goes back on the shelf and what goes in the skip.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the call.

options.label: Let an engineer salvage what's sound

outcomes.headline: {name} saved the good parts
outcomes.text: {name} tested every part before passing it, and saved the team a month of rebuilding.

outcomes.headline: A weakened part slipped back
outcomes.text: {name} passed a valve that looked fine. The heat had softened its spring, and it failed in the next test.

outcomes.headline: Everything in the skip
outcomes.text: The whole unit is scrapped. Safe, if wasteful.

decisions.headline: Who reads the old tapes?
decisions.text: There are crates of recorded data from earlier tests that nobody has ever had time to read properly. An engineer with a free month could go through them, looking for anything odd.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the chance of spotting something.

outcomes.headline: {name} saw a pattern
outcomes.text: Across forty tests, {name} noticed a small spike that always came two seconds before trouble. It becomes an early warning.

outcomes.headline: {name} found nothing
outcomes.text: A month of tapes, and nothing new. {name} came out of it knowing the hardware better, at least.

outcomes.headline: Back in the store
outcomes.text: The crates stay where they are.

decisions.headline: Who runs the thruster firings?
decisions.text: The craft's small thrusters are ready for their first firings in a vacuum cell. The propellant is poisonous, and the test has to be run by someone who knows when to stop.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the chance of a clean set of firings.

outcomes.headline: {name} ran a clean campaign
outcomes.text: {name} fired each thruster thousands of short pulses and caught one valve that stuck open for a few milliseconds. It's changed before it can stick for longer.

outcomes.headline: A leak in the cell
outcomes.text: {name} missed a weeping fitting. The cell had to be cleared and cleaned, and the firings were cut short.

options.label: Nobody, the firings are put off

outcomes.headline: Firings put off
outcomes.text: The thrusters wait in their crates.

decisions.headline: Who runs the separation test?
decisions.text: Two stages are hung in a test frame to be blown apart, as they will be in flight. The rig is expensive and there is only one test set. Someone has to decide when everything is truly ready.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the chance of a clean separation.

outcomes.headline: A clean break
outcomes.text: {name} held the test a day to fix a snagging cable. When the bolts fired, the stages parted cleanly, and the cameras show exactly how.

outcomes.headline: A snagged cable
outcomes.text: {name} fired it on schedule. A cable snagged and tore loose, and the test only proved that cables snag.

options.label: Nobody, the test is put off

outcomes.headline: Put off
outcomes.text: The rig stays hung in its frame.

decisions.headline: Who represents us at the planning meeting?
decisions.text: Every program wants time on the shared test facilities next season, and the schedule is decided at one long meeting. Whoever goes needs to know exactly what the team needs, and why.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the case they make.

outcomes.headline: {name} won the slots
outcomes.text: {name} came armed with test plans and numbers, and came back with twice the facility time the team expected.

outcomes.headline: {name} was outplayed
outcomes.text: Other programs sent smoother talkers. {name} came back with the slots nobody else wanted.

options.label: Let the planning office handle it

outcomes.headline: The usual share
outcomes.text: The planning office gets the team its usual share.

decisions.headline: Who checks the sequencer?
decisions.text: The timer that sends the hardware its commands in flight is set by hand: when to switch on, fire, separate. A single wrong setting would do the wrong thing at the worst moment. Someone has to check every one against the plan.
decisions.stakes: The better the engineer in this component's skill, the better the chance a wrong setting is found.

outcomes.headline: {name} found a wrong second
outcomes.text: {name} found one command set a second too early: it would have fired before the step before it finished. A second, and a mission.

outcomes.headline: {name} changed the wrong one
outcomes.text: {name} 'corrected' a setting that was right. The next ground test went out of order.

options.label: Trust the people who set it

outcomes.headline: As set
outcomes.text: The sequencer stays as it was set.

decisions.headline: Freeze the design?
decisions.text: The chief designer wants to stop changing the drawings and build what's there. The engineers say the open issues will cost something now, but the work would go faster after.

options.label: Freeze the design
options.shows: About a season's gain lost now, then R&D 30 % faster for four seasons.

outcomes.headline: The design is frozen
outcomes.text: The open issues are written up and set aside. The workshops start building to one set of drawings.

options.label: Start a redesign
options.shows: About a season and a half's gain lost now, then R&D 40 % faster for six seasons.

outcomes.headline: Back to the drawing board
outcomes.text: The team throws out the weak parts of the design and starts them again, properly.

outcomes.headline: Refining as before
outcomes.text: The drawings keep changing week by week.

decisions.headline: A sprint on overtime?
decisions.text: The team could work evenings and weekends for a while. The hardware would move faster; the people would get tired.

options.label: Go on overtime
options.shows: R&D 50 % faster for two seasons; the team's morale drops.

outcomes.headline: Lights on all night
outcomes.text: The workshop never closes. The work races ahead, and the coffee runs out by Thursday.

outcomes.headline: Normal hours
outcomes.text: The team goes home on time.

decisions.headline: Hire engineers on contract?
decisions.text: An aircraft firm between projects offers a dozen experienced engineers on contract. They would cost real money, and they'd need a few weeks to learn the hardware, but there would be a lot more hands.

outcomes.headline: A dozen more desks
outcomes.text: The contractors move into a temporary hut behind the workshop and are soon indispensable.

outcomes.headline: A short push
outcomes.text: Just as the contractors learn their way round, they're gone again. But the push helped.

outcomes.headline: No contractors
outcomes.text: The aircraft firm finds other work for its engineers.

decisions.headline: Stop and write it all down?
decisions.text: Half of what the team knows lives in people's heads and notebooks. The chief engineer wants the team to stop for a while and write it all down properly: every test, every change, every reason.

options.label: Stop and write it down
options.shows: About a season and a half's gain now, then R&D 20 % slower for three seasons.

outcomes.headline: A shelf of binders
outcomes.text: Writing it down turns up three contradictions and a test nobody remembers running. Everyone hates it, and everyone is glad it's done.

options.label: Write it down as we go

outcomes.headline: As we go
outcomes.text: The notebooks stay in people's desks.

decisions.headline: Start a second shift?
decisions.text: The workshop sits empty every night. A second shift would keep it busy round the clock, but it needs paying, and the day shift would have to hand its work over every evening.

options.label: Start a second shift
options.shows: R&D 40 % faster for three seasons; the team's morale drops.

outcomes.headline: The lights stay on
outcomes.text: Work goes on round the clock. The handover notes get longer, and tempers shorter.

outcomes.headline: One shift
outcomes.text: The workshop closes at six, as always.

decisions.headline: Sell the test data?
decisions.text: An aircraft builder wants the team's test data on materials and joints, and will pay well for it out of its own budget. Preparing it for outsiders would take engineers away from the work for a while.

options.label: Sell it
options.shows: About a third of a season's funding in; R&D 20 % slower for two seasons.

outcomes.headline: Data for sale
outcomes.text: Two engineers spend weeks cleaning up old records for the buyer. The money is welcome.

outcomes.headline: Not for sale
outcomes.text: The data stays in the agency's files.

decisions.headline: Have a factory build part of it?
decisions.text: A large factory could take over building one of the subassemblies, freeing the team to work on the rest. The factory is fast, but its people have never built anything like it.

options.label: Give the factory the job
options.shows: About half a season's gain lost now, then R&D 30 % faster for four seasons.

outcomes.headline: Built elsewhere
outcomes.text: The first units from the factory need reworking, but after that they come quickly and the team gets on with its own work.

outcomes.headline: Built here
outcomes.text: The team keeps building everything itself.

decisions.headline: Buy the big milling machine?
decisions.text: The workshop wants a large new milling machine that cuts in hours what the old ones take days over. It's expensive, it takes a while to set up, and it would pay for itself only slowly.

outcomes.headline: The new machine arrives
outcomes.text: It takes a crane and a week to install. After that, parts that took days come off it before lunch.

outcomes.headline: Borrowed time
outcomes.text: Parts go out by van to a firm across town and come back faster than the old machines could make them.

outcomes.headline: The old machines
outcomes.text: The old machines keep grinding away.

decisions.headline: Catalogue parts or custom ones?
decisions.text: Many small parts, the valves, switches and fittings, are made to order. The purchasing office says catalogue parts would do nearly as well for much less. The engineers say 'nearly' is the problem.

options.label: Switch to catalogue parts
options.shows: About a fifth of a season's funding saved; about half a season's gain lost.

outcomes.headline: Off the shelf
outcomes.text: The new parts arrive in days, not months, and cost a fraction. A few of them don't quite fit.

outcomes.headline: Made to measure
outcomes.text: Every part made to the drawings and tested on arrival. Expensive, and better.

outcomes.headline: As it is
outcomes.text: The purchasing office sighs and files its report.

decisions.headline: Ease off for a while?
decisions.text: The team has been running hot for months: long days, cancelled holidays, short tempers. The personnel office suggests easing off, with normal hours and the leave people are owed.

options.label: Ease off
options.shows: The team's morale rises; R&D 20 % slower for two seasons.

outcomes.headline: Holidays at last
outcomes.text: People take their leave and come back with suntans and photographs. The work slows, and the mood lifts.

outcomes.headline: Still running hot
outcomes.text: The holidays are put off again.

decisions.headline: Add backups to the vital parts?
decisions.text: The reliability engineers want a second unit for each of the parts the whole thing depends on. It would be safer, but heavier and more complicated, and every test would have to check both.

options.label: Add the backups
options.shows: About two seasons' gain now, then R&D 20 % slower for four seasons.

outcomes.headline: Two of everything vital
outcomes.text: The vital parts are doubled. The design is safer, and the test plans are twice as long.

outcomes.headline: One of each
outcomes.text: The design stays as it is.

decisions.headline: Strip out the clever bit?
decisions.text: One feature of the design is very clever and very fussy: it fails a test about once a month. It's also the pride of the engineer who invented it. Without it the design would be plainer, and easier to get right.

options.label: Strip it out
options.shows: About a season's gain, then R&D 20 % faster for three seasons; the team's morale drops.

outcomes.headline: Plainer and better
outcomes.text: The fussy feature is replaced by something dull that just works. Its inventor takes it personally.

outcomes.headline: Still clever, still fussy
outcomes.text: The clever feature stays, and so do its monthly failures.

decisions.headline: Finish the work at the launch site?
decisions.text: Much of the work could be done at the launch site instead of the factory, saving the long journey back and forth after every change. But the site is remote, and the team would be living in huts far from home.

options.label: Move the team to the site
options.shows: R&D 30 % faster for three seasons; the team's morale drops.

outcomes.headline: Life in the huts
outcomes.text: Changes that took a month of shipping now take a day. The team misses its families and the cinema.

outcomes.headline: Home every night
outcomes.text: The hardware keeps travelling back and forth.

decisions.headline: Put sensors on everything?
decisions.text: Most tests record a handful of readings. The instrumentation lab offers to fit every test with dozens more sensors, so each test teaches more. It means more wiring, more setup and more money.

outcomes.headline: Every test, fully wired
outcomes.text: Each test now produces a stack of charts, and the answers in them come faster than the old way of testing again and again.

outcomes.headline: A few more sensors
outcomes.text: The big tests get the extra sensors, and the small ones carry on as before.

outcomes.headline: The usual readings
outcomes.text: The tests go on with their handful of gauges.

decisions.headline: Build the production tooling now?
decisions.text: The production engineers want to start building the big jigs and fixtures now, before the design has settled, so there's no wait when it does. If the design changes, some of the tooling will be wrong.

options.label: Start the tooling now
options.shows: About half a season's gain lost now, then R&D 35 % faster for three seasons.

outcomes.headline: Jigs before drawings
outcomes.text: The tooling goes up while the drawings are still moving. Some of it has to be cut and rewelded, but the stages start coming together much sooner.

outcomes.headline: Drawings first
outcomes.text: The tooling waits for final drawings.

decisions.headline: Leave one instrument out?
decisions.text: One of the craft's instruments has given more trouble than all the others together. The scientists who built it are proud of it, and their institute paid for part of the craft. Leaving it out would make everything simpler.

options.label: Leave it out
options.shows: The institute's share is paid back; about a season and a half's gain, then R&D 15 % faster for three seasons.

outcomes.headline: One instrument fewer
outcomes.text: With the troublesome instrument gone, the wiring is simpler and the power budget easier. The institute takes its money back, and its scientists stop returning calls.

outcomes.headline: Still aboard
outcomes.text: The instrument stays, and so does the trouble.

decisions.headline: Rebuild the electronics in boxes?
decisions.text: The craft's electronics are wired in place, so changing anything means unsoldering half the craft. The engineers propose rebuilding them as sealed boxes with plugs, each one swapped and tested on its own.

options.label: Rebuild them in boxes
options.shows: About a season's gain lost now, then R&D 35 % faster for five seasons.

outcomes.headline: Unplug, swap, test
outcomes.text: For a season the craft is in pieces. After that, a faulty box comes out in minutes and a better one goes in.

outcomes.headline: Wired in
outcomes.text: The soldering irons stay busy.

decisions.headline: Wrap the electronics in more shielding?
decisions.text: The electronics engineers want thicker metal boxes around everything, against heat, cold and radiation. The structures team says the extra weight means redoing their sums for every bracket.

options.label: Add the shielding
options.shows: About a season and a half's gain now, then R&D 15 % slower for three seasons.

outcomes.headline: Heavier, tougher
outcomes.text: The electronics are snug in thick boxes. The structures team redoes its sums, slowly and with feeling.

outcomes.headline: Light as it is
outcomes.text: The boxes stay thin.

decisions.headline: Test it whole, not stage by stage?
decisions.text: The plan is to prove each stage on its own before testing them together. A bolder plan would test the whole rocket together from the start: fewer tests, but every one of them riskier.

options.label: Test it whole from now on
options.shows: About a season's gain lost now, then R&D 50 % faster for three seasons.

outcomes.headline: Everything at once
outcomes.text: The step-by-step test plan is torn up. The first combined test is rough, but each one after it answers questions for every stage at once.

outcomes.headline: One stage at a time
outcomes.text: The test plan stays as written.

decisions.headline: Shutdown at second 41
decisions.text: On the last test firing the engine shut itself down 41 seconds into a 60-second run. The engineers have three clues and three suspects.

clues.text: Chamber pressure fell steadily for two seconds before the shutdown.
Turbopump vibration stayed normal the whole run.
The igniter fired twice at the start before the engine lit.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: Not the bearing
outcomes.text: The pump comes apart in perfect shape. The vibration data said so all along.

outcomes.headline: The valve it was
outcomes.text: A spring in the fuel valve was too weak and let it drift shut. Falling pressure, then shutdown: it fits. A stiffer spring fixes it.

outcomes.headline: A red herring
outcomes.text: The double ignition was harmless; the engine lit fine. The team loses a season rebuilding an igniter that worked.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The fault stays open until the next firing.

decisions.headline: The battery dies in the chamber
decisions.text: In the vacuum chamber the craft's power fails after a few hours. On the bench it runs for days. The engineers have four clues.

clues.text: The battery holds its voltage for days at room temperature.
In the chamber the voltage sags after the third hour, as the craft cools.
The heater's thermostat is mounted right beside the warm transmitter.
The transmitter draws its normal current throughout.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The cells were fine
outcomes.text: New cells fail the same way. The bench test had already cleared them.

outcomes.headline: It was freezing
outcomes.text: The thermostat sat by the warm transmitter, so it never switched the heater on, and the cold battery gave out. Moving it fixes the craft.

outcomes.headline: Not the radio
outcomes.text: The radio's current was normal all along. A redesigned transmitter changes nothing.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The fault stays open until the next chamber run.

decisions.headline: The shaking stage
decisions.text: Near the end of the last firing the whole stage began to shake lengthwise at a steady beat, harder and harder until the run was cut. The engineers have four clues and three suspects.

clues.text: Chamber pressure and the pressure in the fuel line rose and fell in step, at the same beat as the shaking.
The beat matched the stage's own natural bounce, which quickens as the tanks empty.
The engine mounts were tight and undamaged after the run.
At teardown the turbopump turned smoothly by hand, its bearings like new.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The mounts were fine
outcomes.text: The mounts are rebuilt stiffer, and the next firing shakes just the same. The inspection had said so.

options.label: The engine and the fuel line feeding each other's shaking

outcomes.headline: A loop of shaking
outcomes.text: The stage bounces, the fuel flow surges, the thrust surges, and the stage bounces harder. A gas-filled damper in the fuel line breaks the loop.

outcomes.headline: Not the bearing
outcomes.text: New bearings go in, and the shaking comes back. The old ones were like new.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The fault stays open until the next firing.

decisions.headline: A bang at ignition
decisions.text: The engine lit with a bang that cracked its nozzle. It has started cleanly a dozen times before. Three suspects, three clues.

clues.text: The valves opened on their normal timing, to the hundredth of a second.
The flame came 0.6 seconds after the propellant began to flow. On good starts it comes after 0.1.
The nozzle was X-rayed before the run and was free of cracks.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

options.label: The valves opened out of order

outcomes.headline: The valves were on time
outcomes.text: The valve sequence is redesigned, and nothing changes. The timing record was right all along.

options.label: A flaw in the nozzle from the factory

outcomes.headline: No flaw
outcomes.text: The nozzle supplier is audited and found blameless. The X-ray had already cleared it.

options.label: A weak igniter let propellant pool before it lit

outcomes.headline: A pool, then a bang
outcomes.text: The igniter was weak, so propellant collected in the chamber for half a second and then went up all at once. A hotter igniter fixes it.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The engine waits for a new nozzle and another start.

decisions.headline: Drifting to the left
decisions.text: On the last test flight the rocket drifted steadily left of its path during the climb. The steering caught it in the end, but only just. The engineers have three clues.

clues.text: The drift grew at a steady rate from the moment of liftoff, long before the rocket reached the high winds.
Every steering command was carried out correctly and on time.
The gyroscope unit was replaced the week before the flight, by a new crew.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: Not the wind
outcomes.text: The launch rules for wind are tightened, and the next flight drifts anyway. It drifted from liftoff, before any wind could push it.

outcomes.headline: A degree out
outcomes.text: The new gyroscope unit sat a fraction of a degree crooked in its mount. The rocket steered faithfully along a line that was wrong from the start. A locating pin fixes it.

outcomes.headline: The actuators were fine
outcomes.text: The actuators are stripped and rebuilt for nothing. They had obeyed every command.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The question waits for the next flight.

decisions.headline: The pressure keeps falling
decisions.text: During a long hold on the pad, the pressure in the oxidiser tank kept sagging and the pressurisation had to work hard to keep up. The engineers have three clues.

clues.text: The pressure fell fastest right after each top-up with fresh, cold liquid oxygen.
Leak detectors around every joint and valve on the tank found nothing.
The pressurising gas flowed in at its normal rate whenever it was called for.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: No leak
outcomes.text: Every joint is taken apart and resealed, and the pressure sags just the same. The detectors had found nothing.

outcomes.headline: The regulator was fine
outcomes.text: A new regulator changes nothing. The gas had been flowing normally all along.

options.label: The cold top-ups chill and shrink the gas above the liquid

outcomes.headline: Cold gas, low pressure
outcomes.text: Every top-up chilled the gas in the top of the tank, and cold gas presses less. A warmer pressurising gas and a smarter top-up schedule fix it.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The fault waits for the next long hold.

decisions.headline: A bump at separation
decisions.text: On the last test flight the spent lower stage bumped into the upper one just after they parted, and the upper stage tumbled for a moment before its steering caught it. Three clues.

clues.text: Every separation bolt sent its 'fired' signal at the same instant.
The upper stage's engine lit exactly on time.
After its shutdown command, the lower stage's thrust tailed off slowly over two seconds instead of dropping at once.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The bolts were fine
outcomes.text: A new bolt design is ordered and tested for a season. All the bolts had fired together.

options.label: The lower stage's engine kept pushing after shutdown

outcomes.headline: A push from behind
outcomes.text: Propellant left in the lines kept burning after shutdown and drove the empty stage forward into the other. A short delay before separation, and small rockets to pull the stages apart, fix it.

options.label: The upper stage lit too late

outcomes.headline: It lit on time
outcomes.text: The ignition timing is rearranged, and the next separation bumps just the same.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The bump waits for the next flight.

decisions.headline: The pump ran away
decisions.text: On a short test firing the turbopump suddenly raced far past its limit and the run was cut automatically. Four clues.

clues.text: The pressure at the pump's inlet dropped sharply a moment before it raced.
The hot gas driving the turbine flowed steadily throughout.
For this short test the tank was filled only a quarter full.
At teardown the pump turned freely by hand.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The gas was steady
outcomes.text: The gas generator is rebuilt and the next short test races just the same.

outcomes.headline: Nothing seized
outcomes.text: A seized bearing would slow a pump, not race it, and this one turned freely. A season goes on new bearings.

options.label: The low tank let the pump gulp gas instead of liquid

outcomes.headline: A gulp of gas
outcomes.text: With the tank so low, a whirlpool formed over the outlet and the pump swallowed gas. With nothing to push against, it raced. A baffle over the outlet stops the whirlpool.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The pump waits for the next firing.

decisions.headline: The engine screamed
decisions.text: Twenty seconds into a firing the engine let out a shriek, and the run was stopped. The face of the injector, where the propellants spray in, is badly eroded. Three clues.

clues.text: Chamber pressure began swinging up and down thousands of times a second, starting suddenly.
The chamber walls are intact; only the injector face is eroded, in rings.
Samples of both propellants from the run tested clean.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The propellant was clean
outcomes.text: New filters go in everywhere, and the next engine shrieks too. The samples had been clean.

options.label: A crack in the chamber wall

outcomes.headline: No crack
outcomes.text: The chamber walls are X-rayed inch by inch. They were intact, as the inspection said.

options.label: A pressure wave growing in the chamber, fed by the injector's spray

outcomes.headline: A wave that fed itself
outcomes.text: Each pressure wave made the spray burn harder, which made the next wave stronger. Short walls across the injector face break up the waves.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The engine waits for a new injector and another firing.

decisions.headline: A slow spin
decisions.text: On a test flight the craft began to turn, slowly at first, then a little faster every hour, though nobody had told it to. Three clues.

clues.text: The spin built up at a steady rate, always in the same direction.
The steering gas pressure fell slowly the whole time, though no jet had been commanded.
No command was sent to the craft during those hours.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

options.label: A stray command from the ground

outcomes.headline: Nobody sent anything
outcomes.text: The ground station's procedures are rewritten for nothing. The log showed no commands.

outcomes.headline: A leaky valve
outcomes.text: One valve didn't quite close, and a trickle of gas pushed the craft round like a tiny, endless jet. A better valve seat fixes it.

outcomes.headline: Too slow for that
outcomes.text: A jet stuck open would have spun the craft up in minutes and emptied the tank. This was a trickle. The jets are redesigned to no purpose.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The fault waits for the next flight.

decisions.headline: Too hot on one side
decisions.text: In the sun simulator, a chamber with banks of bright lamps, the craft's electronics overheat. The same craft passed the same test last year. Four clues.

clues.text: The temperature climbs only while one particular side faces the lamps.
The white paint on that side has yellowed since last year's tests.
The electronics draw their normal power.
The heater's switch stayed off throughout the test.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

options.label: The electronics draw too much power

outcomes.headline: Normal power
outcomes.text: The electronics are redesigned to draw less, and the side still cooks. Their power had been normal.

outcomes.headline: The heater was off
outcomes.text: The heater circuit is rewired, and nothing changes. Its switch had stayed off.

options.label: The yellowed paint soaks up more sunlight

outcomes.headline: Darker paint, hotter craft
outcomes.text: Paint that has yellowed under the lamps absorbs more light and reflects less. A paint that keeps its white fixes it.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The fault waits for the next run in the simulator.

decisions.headline: A fog on the lens
decisions.text: After two weeks in the vacuum chamber, the craft's camera lens is covered in a faint haze, and its pictures are blurred. Four clues.

clues.text: The haze is a thin, oily film on the inside of the lens.
The seal around the lens is intact.
The lens was never colder than the rest of the craft.
New cable insulation went in last month, a plastic not on the approved list.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

options.label: Water condensing on a cold lens

outcomes.headline: Not water
outcomes.text: A lens heater is designed and fitted, and the haze comes back. The film was oily, and the lens was never cold.

options.label: Dust getting in past the seal

outcomes.headline: The seal held
outcomes.text: A new seal is designed for a seal that worked.

options.label: The new plastic giving off vapour in the vacuum

outcomes.headline: The plastic was breathing
outcomes.text: In a vacuum, some plastics give off vapour that settles on the nearest cool, clean surface: the lens. The insulation goes back to the approved kind.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The lens is cleaned, and the question waits.

decisions.headline: A command nobody sent
decisions.text: In a long ground test, the craft switched off one of its instruments by itself, as if commanded to. It has happened three times now. Four clues.

clues.text: No command went out from the test console at those times.
Each time, the craft's heater had just switched on.
On the bench, the command receiver rejects every garbled command thrown at it.
The heater's power wires run in the same bundle as the command lines.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

options.label: A fault in the test console

outcomes.headline: The console was silent
outcomes.text: The console is rebuilt, and the craft does it again. The log had shown nothing sent.

options.label: The heater's switching surge leaking into the command lines

outcomes.headline: A spark in the bundle
outcomes.text: Each time the heater switched on, the surge jumped across to the command lines beside it, just enough to look like a command. Separate bundles and a filter fix it.

outcomes.headline: The receiver was fine
outcomes.text: A new receiver is built, and the instrument still switches itself off. The bench test had cleared the old one.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The test goes on, and the instrument is switched back on by hand.

decisions.headline: The boom won't unfold
decisions.text: The craft's instrument boom unfolds every time on the bench, but in the cold vacuum chamber it stayed folded. Four clues.

clues.text: On the bench, at room temperature, the boom springs open every time.
In the chamber, the release charge fired and its signal came back.
The grease in the hinge was stiff as wax when the chamber was opened.
Once warmed up, the hinge turned freely, metal on metal unharmed.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: It fired
outcomes.text: A stronger charge is designed and tested for a season. The old one had fired, and said so.

options.label: The hinge's metal surfaces stuck together in the vacuum

outcomes.headline: No sticking
outcomes.text: It can happen in a vacuum, but this hinge turned freely once warmed, its surfaces unharmed. A coated hinge is made for nothing.

options.label: The grease stiffened in the cold

outcomes.headline: Grease like wax
outcomes.text: The ordinary grease turned stiff in the cold and held the spring back. A grease made for cold and vacuum fixes it.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The boom waits for the next chamber run.

decisions.headline: Garbled playback
decisions.text: The craft stores its readings on a small tape recorder and plays them back over each ground station. After a few days in the vacuum chamber, the playback came out garbled. Four clues.

clues.text: The recorder's motor kept a steady speed throughout.
The tape's edges have curled and stretched.
The recording heads are smooth and barely worn.
To save weight, the tape was changed last month for a thinner kind.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The motor was steady
outcomes.text: A new motor controller is built, and the playback is still garbled.

options.label: The thinner tape stretching in the vacuum

outcomes.headline: The wrong tape
outcomes.text: The thin tape stretched and curled in the vacuum and warmth, so it ran crooked past the heads. The old tape goes back in, weight and all.

outcomes.headline: The heads were fine
outcomes.text: New heads go in, and the playback is just as bad. The old ones were barely worn.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The recorder waits for the next chamber run.

decisions.headline: The panels fade
decisions.text: Under the sun lamps the craft's solar panels give their full power at first, then less and less as the test goes on. Four clues.

clues.text: The output falls as the panels warm up, and recovers when the lamps go off for a while.
Every cell met its rating before it was mounted.
All the panels fade together, by the same amount.
The panels are mounted flat against the craft's body, with no gap behind them.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The cells were good
outcomes.text: Every panel is rebuilt with new cells, and they fade just the same.

options.label: A bad joint in the panel wiring

outcomes.headline: Not the wiring
outcomes.text: One bad joint would dim one panel, not all of them together. The rewiring changes nothing.

options.label: The cells get too hot to work well

outcomes.headline: Too warm to work
outcomes.text: Solar cells give less power the hotter they get, and these had nowhere to lose their heat. A gap behind the panels lets them cool.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The panels wait for the next run under the lamps.

decisions.headline: Only when it's shaken
decisions.text: One reading keeps dropping out during the vibration tests, then comes back. It never happens anywhere else. Four clues.

clues.text: The dropouts come only when the shake table runs at one particular frequency.
The sensor passes every bench test.
The other channels on the same recorder never drop out.
The pins of the sensor's connector show tiny polished rub marks.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The sensor was fine
outcomes.text: A new sensor drops out just like the old one, which passed every bench test.

outcomes.headline: Not the recorder
outcomes.text: The recorder is overhauled for nothing. Its other channels never dropped a reading.

outcomes.headline: A connector that chattered
outcomes.text: At one frequency the connector rattled just enough to break contact for an instant. A locking connector and a clamp on the cable fix it.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The fault waits for the next shake test.

decisions.headline: A white crust
decisions.text: After a month in storage at the launch site, by the sea, some aluminium parts are pitted under a white crust. Others from the same batch, in the same shed, are fine. Three clues.

clues.text: The crust is only where the aluminium touches steel bolts and brackets.
The batch certificate is in order, and untouched parts from the batch are unharmed.
The shed's air is damp and salty, as it always is on the coast.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: Not the air alone
outcomes.text: The shed is fitted with dehumidifiers, at a cost, and the crust still forms where steel meets aluminium. The other parts had breathed the same air.

outcomes.headline: The batch was good
outcomes.text: The supplier is asked for a new batch, which pits in the same places.

options.label: Two different metals touching in damp air

outcomes.headline: Two metals, one battery
outcomes.text: Where steel touches aluminium in damp, salty air, the pair works like a tiny battery and eats the aluminium. Insulating washers and a coating fix it.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The parts are cleaned, and the question waits.

decisions.headline: A glitch at noon
decisions.text: Every day of a long test, the readings jump at about noon for a few minutes, then settle. The test hall has no windows. Four clues.

clues.text: The jumps come at noon every day, give or take a few minutes, weekends included.
One spare channel with nothing connected to it jumps too.
The canteen's big ovens next door are on the same power line, and lunch is cooked all week.
The recorders' power supplies have no filters.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The hardware was innocent
outcomes.text: A season goes on hunting a fault in the hardware. A channel with nothing on it had jumped too.

options.label: The midday sun heating the test hall

outcomes.headline: No sun in there
outcomes.text: The hall gets new insulation, and noon brings the same jumps. It has no windows.

options.label: The canteen ovens disturbing the power

outcomes.headline: Lunch was on
outcomes.text: The ovens switching on shook the power line, and the unfiltered recorders wrote it down as data. Filters fix it, and a month of odd readings make sense at last.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: Noon comes round again tomorrow.

decisions.headline: Loose after shaking
decisions.text: After a routine vibration test, several bolts were found loose. The test is supposed to find weak designs, not loose bolts. Four clues.

clues.text: The shake table ran at its normal levels, no harder than the launch.
Every loose bolt is the right part, from the approved store.
All the loose bolts are on one panel, fitted by the same shift.
That shift's torque wrench was last checked two years ago.

decisions.stakes: The right cause is worth about two seasons' gain; chasing the wrong one costs a season's.

outcomes.headline: The test was normal
outcomes.text: The test levels are turned down, and the hardware is tested more gently than it will fly.

outcomes.headline: The right bolts
outcomes.text: The store is audited for a month and found in order.

options.label: The bolts were never tight enough

outcomes.headline: A wrench that lied
outcomes.text: The old torque wrench read high, so every bolt that shift fitted was under-tightened. Every wrench in the building is checked, and two more are out.

outcomes.headline: More data first
outcomes.text: The bolts are tightened and the question waits.

decisions.headline: The air force lends its altitude chamber
decisions.text: The air force offers its high-altitude test chamber for a month. The catch: it wants one of the team's engineers on loan for two seasons in return.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Accept, and send an engineer
options.shows: About three seasons' gain at once; the engineer is away for two seasons.

outcomes.headline: A month at altitude
outcomes.text: The chamber shows what a month of tests at home never could. {name} packs a bag for the air base.

outcomes.headline: Thanks, but no
outcomes.text: The chamber goes to someone else.

decisions.headline: A cheaper part, untested
decisions.text: A new supplier offers a part at a third of the usual price, available now. Nobody has flown it yet.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Take the cheaper part
options.shows: Saves money; 60 % chance it works out, else about a season and a half's gain lost.

outcomes.headline: It works as well as the old one
outcomes.text: The new part passes every test, and the savings go back into the budget.

outcomes.headline: You get what you pay for
outcomes.text: The part fails its third test. The old supplier has to be called back, at the old price and with a delay.

outcomes.headline: The usual supplier
outcomes.text: The usual parts arrive at the usual price.

decisions.headline: Two students for a season
decisions.text: A university offers two of its best research students for a season, unpaid. The catch: somebody on the team will have to look after them, and students take looking after.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Take the students
options.shows: 60 % chance of about a season and a half's gain; else R&D 15 % slower for two seasons.

outcomes.headline: Sharper than expected
outcomes.text: The students ask naive questions, and two of them turn out not to be naive at all.

outcomes.headline: A season of hand-holding
outcomes.text: The students mean well, but the team spends more time teaching them than working.

outcomes.headline: Not this year
outcomes.text: The students go to an aircraft firm instead.

decisions.headline: A test lab's sale
decisions.text: A military lab is closing and offering its test equipment to anyone who pays to move it: recorders, gauges, a small shake table. Whatever isn't collected by the end of the month goes for scrap.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Buy a truckload
options.shows: 70 % chance of about two seasons' gain, else about half a season's.

outcomes.headline: Treasure in the crates
outcomes.text: Most of it works, and some of it is better than anything the team owns. The test lab gets a lot busier.

outcomes.headline: Mostly junk
outcomes.text: Most of the crates hold broken or obsolete gear. A few gauges are worth keeping.

outcomes.headline: Scrapped
outcomes.text: The equipment goes to the scrapyard.

decisions.headline: Fish the stage out of the sea?
decisions.text: A salvage ship working off the coast could look for the spent stage from the last test flight, which came down in shallow water. Hardware that has really flown tells things no ground test can. The ship leaves at the end of the month.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Hire the ship
options.shows: 60 % chance of about two and a half seasons' gain, else nothing.

outcomes.headline: Up from the seabed
outcomes.text: Divers find the stage broken but recognisable. Scorch marks on its base show where hot gas had been leaking during the climb.

outcomes.headline: Nothing but sand
outcomes.text: Two weeks of searching in murky water, and the stage was never found.

outcomes.headline: Left to the fish
outcomes.text: The stage stays where it fell.

decisions.headline: An exchange abroad
decisions.text: The engineers of a friendly country's space program invite one of the team to work with them for a season. Whoever goes will learn a lot, and will be missed.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Send an engineer
options.shows: The engineer is away for a season; 70 % chance of about a season's gain and a much better engineer back.

outcomes.headline: {name} came back full of ideas
outcomes.text: {name} writes home every week with tricks the hosts use, and comes back a better engineer.

outcomes.headline: A season of sightseeing
outcomes.text: The hosts kept {name} busy with dinners and tours, and very far from their hardware.

outcomes.headline: Perhaps next year
outcomes.text: The invitation is politely declined.

decisions.headline: A troubled program asks for help
decisions.text: Another program in the agency is in trouble and asks to borrow one engineer from the team for two seasons. In return it offers its whole test archive, which the team has wanted for years.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Lend an engineer
options.shows: About a season and a half's gain at once; the engineer is away for two seasons.

outcomes.headline: An archive for an engineer
outcomes.text: The archive arrives by the truckload and answers questions the team was about to spend months on. {name} goes off to fight someone else's fires.

outcomes.headline: Nobody to spare
outcomes.text: The other program finds help elsewhere.

decisions.headline: A film crew wants the workshop
decisions.text: A film studio is making a picture about spaceflight and wants to shoot in the real workshop for a few weeks. It pays very well. It also means lights, cables and actors among the hardware.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Let them film
options.shows: About a third of a season's funding; R&D 25 % slower for a season, and a small chance of damage.

outcomes.headline: Lights, camera, hardware
outcomes.text: The crew is gone in three weeks, the cheque clears, and two technicians appear as extras.

outcomes.headline: A dolly into a test unit
outcomes.text: A camera dolly ran into a test unit. The studio pays for the repairs, but the unit is weeks behind.

outcomes.headline: No filming
outcomes.text: The studio builds a cardboard workshop instead.

decisions.headline: A great designer, for one season
decisions.text: A celebrated designer, between jobs, will consult on the team's hardware for one season, at a fee to match the reputation. Next season the designer is gone to a bigger project.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Hire the designer
options.shows: 75 % chance of about three seasons' gain, else about a season's.

outcomes.headline: A season of masterclasses
outcomes.text: The designer spends the season walking the workshop, asking why. By the end, the design is simpler and the team is better.

outcomes.headline: Two chiefs
outcomes.text: The designer and the team's lead disagree about everything. Some good advice gets through anyway.

outcomes.headline: Not at that price
outcomes.text: The designer goes to another program.

decisions.headline: The observatory's big dish
decisions.text: A radio observatory is between projects and offers its big dish for a few nights. The craft's transmitter could be tested from a mountain far away, at the faintness it will have in flight. The catch: the craft has to be hauled up the mountain.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Haul the craft up the mountain
options.shows: About two seasons' gain; R&D 20 % slower for a season.

outcomes.headline: A whisper from the mountain
outcomes.text: The dish hears the craft's faint signal across fifty kilometres, and shows exactly where the transmitter loses its margin. The trip took longer than anyone hoped.

outcomes.headline: Not this time
outcomes.text: The observatory goes back to the stars.

decisions.headline: An engineering prize
decisions.text: A national engineering society has opened its annual prize, and the team's latest work would make a strong entry. Writing it up would take the best people off the hardware for a few weeks. Entries close this month.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Enter the competition
options.shows: R&D 15 % slower for a season; a chance at prize money and a proud team.

outcomes.headline: The prize is ours
outcomes.text: The team wins, and the prize money is welcome. So is the dinner.

outcomes.headline: Highly commended
outcomes.text: A certificate, a photograph in the society's journal, and a team that walks a little taller.

outcomes.headline: Not placed
outcomes.text: The prize goes to a bridge. The team pretends not to mind.

outcomes.headline: No entry
outcomes.text: The prize goes to someone else, as it would have anyway.

decisions.headline: The national exhibition
decisions.text: The government wants a real piece of the team's hardware for the centre of its national exhibition, and will pay well for the loan. The test unit would be away for a season, on show to millions.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Lend the test unit
options.shows: About a third of a season's funding; R&D 25 % slower for a season, and a risk of damage on the road.

outcomes.headline: Seen by millions
outcomes.text: Queues round the block, and the team's families take their photographs beside it. It comes home safely.

outcomes.headline: Dropped at the loading bay
outcomes.text: On the way home, the crate slipped off a forklift. The money is welcome; the test unit is a wreck.

outcomes.headline: A fine model
outcomes.text: The exhibition gets a beautiful model, and pays nothing for it.

decisions.headline: The coldest room in the country
decisions.text: A physics institute can cool a chamber far colder than anything the agency owns, colder than the craft will ever see. It's free for a few days this month, but the craft would have to be taken apart to fit through its door.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Take it apart and test it
options.shows: 70 % chance of about two seasons' gain; else about half a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: Colder than space, and working
outcomes.text: At temperatures the craft will never meet, two parts cracked and one switch froze. All three are changed, and the craft goes back together.

outcomes.headline: Broken putting it back
outcomes.text: The test went well, but putting the craft back together went badly: a connector cracked and a panel was bent.

outcomes.headline: In one piece
outcomes.text: The institute's chamber goes back to its physicists.

decisions.headline: Share a test campaign?
decisions.text: A neighbouring program has booked a big test campaign and has room to test the team's hardware too, at no charge. The catch: the team would have to work to the other program's schedule, not its own.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Join their campaign
options.shows: About two seasons' gain; R&D 15 % slower for two seasons.

outcomes.headline: On someone else's schedule
outcomes.text: The tests are excellent, and come at the most awkward possible times.

outcomes.headline: Our own way
outcomes.text: The neighbours test their own hardware.

decisions.headline: A part, months early
decisions.text: A supplier has found spare capacity and can deliver a key part three months early, if the order is changed this month and a premium is paid.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

outcomes.headline: Here already
outcomes.text: The part arrives early and the team can test with it months sooner than planned.

outcomes.headline: On schedule
outcomes.text: The part will come when it comes.

decisions.headline: Engines from a cancelled missile
decisions.text: A missile program has been cancelled, and its spare engines go to whoever pays to ship and store them, this month only. They're close to what the team uses. Close, not the same.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Buy a few for testing
options.shows: 65 % chance of about two and a half seasons' gain; else nothing, and some money back.

outcomes.headline: Close enough to learn from
outcomes.text: The engines are close enough to fire on the team's stand. Firing engines nobody minds wrecking teaches a great deal.

outcomes.headline: Not close enough
outcomes.text: The mountings and the plumbing are all different. The engines go on to another program, which pays back some of the cost.

outcomes.headline: Passed
outcomes.text: Another agency buys them.

decisions.headline: A tracking station on wheels
decisions.text: The tracking network's mobile station, a convoy of lorries with an antenna, is passing nearby this month. Its crew offers to rehearse a whole flight's radio traffic with the craft, if the team works nights to fit their schedule.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Rehearse with them
options.shows: About a season and a half's gain; the team's morale drops.

outcomes.headline: A flight's worth of talk
outcomes.text: A week of nights talking to the craft as if it were in orbit. The station's crew finds three commands that confuse it.

outcomes.headline: The convoy rolls on
outcomes.text: The lorries drive on to their next stop.

decisions.headline: A seat on a research flight
decisions.text: A research aircraft flies high and fast, carrying instruments, and its crew offers a place on board for a test package, plus an engineer to tend it. They'd want the engineer for their own work for a season.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Send a package and an engineer
options.shows: 75 % chance of about two seasons' gain; the engineer is away for a season.

outcomes.headline: {name} flew with it
outcomes.text: The package flew a dozen times, shaken and chilled the way only a real flight can, with {name} tending it in a bulky flight suit.

outcomes.headline: Grounded all season
outcomes.text: The research aircraft spent the season in its hangar with an engine problem. {name} spent it helping fix it.

outcomes.headline: Thanks, but no
outcomes.text: Another team's package takes the seat.

decisions.headline: Machinists looking for work
decisions.text: A tractor works nearby has finished a big order early, and a dozen of its skilled machinists have nothing to do. They could join the workshop for a season, starting next week, on better pay than the workshop's own people.
decisions.stakes: This turn only.

options.label: Take them on
options.shows: R&D 30 % faster for a season; a risk of trouble with the workshop.

outcomes.headline: Extra hands
outcomes.text: The machinists are good, and the workshop's own people are glad of the help.

outcomes.headline: Bad blood
outcomes.text: The workshop's own people resent outsiders paid more than they are. The work speeds up, and the atmosphere sours.

outcomes.headline: Not this time
outcomes.text: The machinists go back to their own works.

decisions.headline: Who works with whom?
decisions.text: A tricky interface between two subsystems needs two engineers who will talk to each other. Pick a pair; how well they get on decides how it goes.
decisions.stakes: A good pair is worth about two seasons' gain and grows closer; a bad one clashes.

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second} cracked it
outcomes.text: {name} and {second} worked it out over two long evenings and came out friends.

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second} clashed
outcomes.text: {name} and {second} argued over every drawing. The interface is still a mess, and so is their working relationship.

options.label: Leave the team as it is

outcomes.headline: As it was
outcomes.text: The interface is worked on in the usual way.

decisions.headline: An old hand and a new one
decisions.text: The training office suggests pairing two engineers for a season so one can learn from the other. It only works if they get along.
decisions.stakes: A good pair is worth about a season's gain and grows closer; a bad one clashes.

outcomes.headline: {second} learned a lot from {name}
outcomes.text: The two spend the season side by side, and the questions get better every week.

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second} didn't get on
outcomes.text: One lectured, the other stopped listening. They ask to be split up.

outcomes.headline: No pairing
outcomes.text: Everyone works as before.

decisions.headline: Two to find the fault
decisions.text: A fault keeps turning up on the night shift and vanishing by day. Two engineers, one from each shift, need to hunt it down together, which means trusting each other's notes.
decisions.stakes: A good pair is worth about two seasons' gain and grows closer; a bad one blames the other shift.

options.label: Put two engineers on the hunt

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second} cornered it
outcomes.text: {name} kept the day's log, {second} the night's, and together the logs showed the fault came with the cold. They found it in a week.

outcomes.headline: Each blamed the other's shift
outcomes.text: {name} and {second} spent the week proving it was the other shift's fault. The fault is still there.

options.label: Let each shift look on its own

outcomes.headline: Separate hunts
outcomes.text: Each shift looks for the fault in its own way.

decisions.headline: Check each other's work
decisions.text: The quality office wants a two-person rule for the critical assembly: every step done by one engineer and checked by another before the next. It only works if the checker speaks up and the other listens.
decisions.stakes: A good pair is worth about a season and a half's gain; a bad one nitpicks and resents.

outcomes.headline: {second} caught what {name} missed
outcomes.text: {second} caught two mistakes in {name}'s work and said so plainly. {name} thanked {second} for it, and meant it.

outcomes.headline: Nitpicking
outcomes.text: {second} questioned every washer, {name} took it personally, and the assembly slowed to a crawl.

outcomes.headline: One pair of eyes
outcomes.text: The assembly goes on as before.

decisions.headline: A long drive to the supplier
decisions.text: A delicate part has to be fetched from a supplier two days' drive away, and nobody trusts a courier with it. Two engineers will make the trip together, with the part between them.
decisions.stakes: Two days in a car: a good pair comes back friends, a bad one barely speaking.

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second}, road friends
outcomes.text: Two days of talk, bad coffee and a puncture fixed together. The part arrived without a scratch, and {name} and {second} came back with a dozen ideas from the supplier's floor.

outcomes.headline: A very quiet car
outcomes.text: By the second morning {name} and {second} had run out of polite things to say. The part arrived fine; they didn't.

outcomes.headline: By courier
outcomes.text: The courier is careful, as it turns out.

decisions.headline: Three nights on watch
decisions.text: An endurance test will run for three days and nights without stopping. Two engineers must take turns at the gauges, waking each other when anything odd shows.
decisions.stakes: A good pair is worth about two seasons' gain and grows closer; a bad one misses things.

outcomes.headline: {name} woke {second} at 3 a.m.
outcomes.text: On the second night {name} saw a reading creep and woke {second}, who knew at once what it meant. They stopped the test just in time to save the unit and learn why.

outcomes.headline: Nobody woke anybody
outcomes.text: {name} didn't want to wake {second} over a small reading, and by morning it wasn't small. The unit was damaged, and so were relations.

outcomes.headline: Watched by machines
outcomes.text: The recorders run all night, and the charts are read in the morning.

decisions.headline: Teach each other
decisions.text: Two engineers know very different corners of the hardware. The training office suggests they spend a season teaching each other, an hour a day, so that neither is the only one who knows.
decisions.stakes: A good pair learns, and the first of them becomes a better engineer; a bad one gives up after a week.

outcomes.headline: {name} learned {second}'s corner
outcomes.text: By the end of the season {name} can do {second}'s job, and the hour a day has turned into lunch together.

outcomes.headline: A week of lessons
outcomes.text: {second} was an impatient teacher and {name} a reluctant pupil. The lessons stopped after a week.

outcomes.headline: Each to their own corner
outcomes.text: Everyone keeps their own knowledge.

decisions.headline: Two in front of the board
decisions.text: The design review board wants the team's case presented by two engineers: one for the design, one for the tests. They must agree on every answer, because the board will look for cracks.
decisions.stakes: A good pair wins the board over; a bad one contradicts itself in public.

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second} held the room
outcomes.text: {name} answered for the design, {second} for the tests, and the board found no daylight between them. The design is approved, with two useful suggestions.

outcomes.headline: Daylight between them
outcomes.text: {name} said one thing and {second} another, in front of the whole board. The review is repeated next season, and the two are not speaking.

outcomes.headline: The lead presents
outcomes.text: The team lead presents, and the board approves with the usual list of questions.

decisions.headline: A bet on the test
decisions.text: Two engineers disagree about how the next test will come out and want to settle it with a bet: loser buys dinner, and both must write down why they think what they think. The team is taking sides.
decisions.stakes: A good pair turns it into a friendly contest; a bad one turns it into a feud.

outcomes.headline: Dinner on {second}
outcomes.text: {name} won, {second} paid up with good grace, and the two write-ups between them explained the test better than the official report.

outcomes.headline: A bet nobody paid
outcomes.text: The test came out halfway between, {name} and {second} both claimed the win, and the team took sides for weeks.

outcomes.headline: No bet
outcomes.text: The test runs without a wager on it.

decisions.headline: One small office, two engineers
decisions.text: While the building is renovated, two engineers will have to share one small office for a season. The facilities office asks who should go in together.
decisions.stakes: A good pair grows close and works faster; a bad one makes a season feel like a year.

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second}'s little office
outcomes.text: Desk to desk, {name} and {second} start finishing each other's calculations. When the renovation ends, they ask to stay together.

outcomes.headline: A long season
outcomes.text: {name} hums; {second} can't stand humming. By the end of the season they're working in the corridor.

outcomes.headline: Sorted by the alphabet
outcomes.text: The facilities office pairs people by surname, and nobody minds much.

decisions.headline: Two to the launch site, tonight
decisions.text: A problem has turned up on the hardware at the launch site, and the people there can't solve it. Two engineers must fly out tonight and fix it, with nobody to ask.
decisions.stakes: High stakes: a good pair is worth about three seasons' gain; a bad one makes it worse.

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second} fixed it
outcomes.text: Thirty hours without sleep, one argument settled in a minute, and the problem was solved. {name} and {second} came home heroes.

outcomes.headline: Two fixes, both wrong
outcomes.text: {name} and {second} each tried their own fix without telling the other. The hardware came home for repairs.

options.label: Talk them through it by telephone
options.shows: Sure to give about half a season's gain.

outcomes.headline: Fixed by telephone
outcomes.text: Three long calls, a crackling line, and a fix that will do for now.

decisions.headline: Dinner to mend a feud?
decisions.text: Two engineers have been snapping at each other for weeks, and the team is tired of it. The team lead suggests you take them both out to dinner and let them talk it through.
decisions.stakes: It works best on a pair who still respect each other; on a bad pair it can make things worse.

options.label: Take two of them to dinner

outcomes.headline: {name} and {second} made peace
outcomes.text: Over the second bottle {name} and {second} found the feud began with a misheard remark months ago. They laughed about it. The team breathes again.

outcomes.headline: A dinner to forget
outcomes.text: {name} brought up an old grievance, {second} left before dessert, and the team heard all about it the next day.

outcomes.headline: Left to themselves
outcomes.text: The snapping goes on, a little quieter.

decisions.headline: The rival's engine runs cooler
decisions.text: The Intelligence Office reports that the rival agency cools its engine by running fuel through the chamber walls before burning it. Our engineers could try the same.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: The tip was good
outcomes.text: Fuel through the walls keeps the chamber cool enough to run longer and harder. The engineers wonder why they didn't think of it.

outcomes.headline: The tip was garbled
outcomes.text: The report mixed up two different engines. The team loses a season on a design that was never going to work.

outcomes.headline: Our own way
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: The rival's craft stays warm
decisions.text: The Intelligence Office says the rival wraps its craft in layers of thin metallised film to keep its warmth in. Our engineers could copy it.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: Wrapped up warm
outcomes.text: Layers of film keep the craft's temperature steady through the night side. The tip was right.

outcomes.headline: Wrong film, wrong place
outcomes.text: The film the report described traps heat where it shouldn't. The electronics overheat in testing.

outcomes.headline: Our own way
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: Why the rival's rocket blew up
decisions.text: The rival's rocket exploded on its pad last month. The Intelligence Office says the cause was a valve frozen shut by ice, and our rocket uses a similar valve.

options.label: Pay to check our valves for the same flaw
options.shows: If the tip is right, about two seasons' gain; if not, only the money is lost.

outcomes.headline: We had it too
outcomes.text: Cold-soaked on a test rig, two of our valves iced shut just as the report said. A small heater cures it.

outcomes.headline: Nothing there
outcomes.text: Our valves stayed free in every test. Either the report was wrong, or the rival's valve isn't like ours after all.

options.label: Redesign the valve straight away
options.shows: If the tip is right, about two seasons' gain; if not, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: Fixed before it could freeze
outcomes.text: The valve gets a heater and a drain. Nobody will ever know if it would have frozen, which is the point.

outcomes.headline: A fix for the wrong fault
outcomes.text: The rival's rocket had failed for some other reason. The redesigned valve brings new teething troubles of its own.

outcomes.headline: Their problem
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: The rival welds by machine
decisions.text: The Intelligence Office has photographs of the rival's tank shop: long machines that weld the seams automatically, with nobody holding a torch. Our tanks are welded by hand.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: Seams like a ruler
outcomes.text: The machine lays a weld as even as a ruled line, every time. The tank shop's reject rate falls to almost nothing.

outcomes.headline: A machine for something else
outcomes.text: The machines in the photographs were cutting, not welding. Ours spoils a dozen tank sections before it is given up.

outcomes.headline: By hand, as before
outcomes.text: The welders keep their torches.

decisions.headline: Gyroscopes on a cushion of air
decisions.text: A source says the rival's new gyroscopes spin on a thin cushion of gas instead of ball bearings, and drift far less. Our guidance team could try to build one.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: Smooth as silk
outcomes.text: With no balls to rattle, the gyroscope barely drifts. The guidance team wants one in everything.

outcomes.headline: It wobbled
outcomes.text: The source left out the hard part. Our gas bearing wobbles, and a season goes into making it work no better than the old one.

outcomes.headline: Ball bearings it is
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: Many small engines
decisions.text: The Intelligence Office believes the rival has stopped building one big engine per stage and clusters several small ones instead, so each engine is easier to test and perfect.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, R&D 30 % faster for four seasons; if it's wrong, about a season and a half's gain lost.

outcomes.headline: Small engines, quick tests
outcomes.text: Small engines are cheap to fire and quick to fix. The test stand fires twice as often, and learns twice as fast.

outcomes.headline: A cluster of problems
outcomes.text: The source had it backwards: the rival was giving up on clusters, not adopting them. Ours bring plumbing troubles that cost a season and a half.

outcomes.headline: Our own engines
outcomes.text: The engine plan stays as it is.

decisions.headline: Separated by springs
decisions.text: According to the Intelligence Office, the rival pushes its stages apart with big springs instead of small rockets: nothing to ignite, nothing to fail.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: A gentle push
outcomes.text: The springs push the stages apart cleanly in every test. Fewer explosives on the rocket, and fewer worries.

outcomes.headline: Not strong enough
outcomes.text: Springs work for the rival's light upper stage, perhaps. Ours barely move the heavy one. The old design goes back in.

outcomes.headline: Rockets it is
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: A checkerboard craft
decisions.text: A photograph shows the rival's craft painted in a pattern of black and white squares. The Intelligence Office thinks the pattern is worked out to keep the inside at an even temperature.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: Paint as a thermostat
outcomes.text: The right mix of black and white holds the craft's insides steady through sun and shadow, with no moving parts at all.

outcomes.headline: Just markings
outcomes.text: The squares were only for the rival's tracking cameras. Our patterned craft runs too cold, and is repainted.

outcomes.headline: Our own paint
outcomes.text: The photograph goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: A lighter battery
decisions.text: The Intelligence Office reports that the rival's craft run on a new kind of battery, much lighter for the power it gives. It names the chemistry, but not the details.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: Half the weight
outcomes.text: The new cells hold as much for half the weight. The spare weight goes into a second battery.

outcomes.headline: A battery that won't last
outcomes.text: The new cells are light, and die after a few dozen charges. Whatever the rival does differently, the report didn't say.

outcomes.headline: Our own batteries
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: An antenna for every direction
decisions.text: The rival's craft, the Intelligence Office says, carries four whip antennas arranged so that it can be heard whichever way it turns. Our craft goes quiet at some angles.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: Heard from every side
outcomes.text: With four antennas set at the right angles, the signal hardly changes as the craft turns. The ground stations are delighted.

outcomes.headline: Four antennas, one muddle
outcomes.text: Without the details of how they're fed, four antennas interfere with each other. The signal is worse than with one.

outcomes.headline: One antenna
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: Air inside the craft
decisions.text: A source says the rival seals its craft's electronics in a shell filled with gas at ground pressure, with a fan to stir it. The electronics never know they've left the ground.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about three seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: A little bit of home
outcomes.text: Inside the sealed shell the stirred gas carries heat away from the electronics as it does on the ground. Parts that worried the team stop worrying it.

outcomes.headline: A slow leak
outcomes.text: Our sealed shell leaks slowly, and keeping it tight costs a season. The source made it sound easy.

outcomes.headline: Open to space
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.
