decisions.headline: The rival's cheap supplier
decisions.text: The Intelligence Office has found that the rival buys a whole class of parts from a small firm at half the price we pay. The firm would sell to us too.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about a third of a season's funding saved; if it's wrong, the savings come with about a season and a half's gain lost.

outcomes.headline: Half the price, same quality
outcomes.text: The small firm's parts pass every test. The savings go back into the budget.

outcomes.headline: Half the price, half the quality
outcomes.text: The firm's parts are cheap for a reason. A third of them fail inspection, and the old supplier has to be begged to come back.

outcomes.headline: Our usual supplier
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: Licensed technicians
decisions.text: According to the Intelligence Office, no rival technician may touch flight hardware without passing an exam and wearing a badge for each skill. Their faults in assembly are said to be rare.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about two seasons' gain; if it's wrong, the team resents a pointless exam.

options.label: Bring in the exams and badges

outcomes.headline: Badges worn with pride
outcomes.text: The technicians grumble at the exams, then wear the badges proudly. Assembly faults fall sharply.

outcomes.headline: Exams for nothing
outcomes.text: The exams test what the technicians already know, and they know it. The faults stay where they were; the goodwill doesn't.

outcomes.headline: No exams
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: One form for every failure
decisions.text: A source describes the rival's failure reports: every fault, however small, written on one form within a day and tracked until it's closed. Ours are scattered across notebooks.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about a season and a half's gain and R&D a little faster for a while; if it's wrong, a lot of paperwork for nothing.

outcomes.headline: Nothing falls through the cracks
outcomes.text: Within a month the forms show the same small fault cropping up in three places. Fixing it once fixes all three.

outcomes.headline: Drowning in forms
outcomes.text: Without whatever else the rival does with them, the forms just pile up. The engineers spend Fridays filling them in.

outcomes.headline: Notebooks, as before
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: A talk that said too much
decisions.text: At an international conference, one of the rival's engineers gave a talk more candid than it should have been. The Intelligence Office has notes, and thinks one remark explains a problem our team is stuck on.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about two seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about half a season's lost.

outcomes.headline: One remark, one answer
outcomes.text: Read the right way, the remark points straight at the cause. The problem is solved in a fortnight.

outcomes.headline: Lost in translation
outcomes.text: The remark meant something else in the speaker's language. A few weeks go on a false trail.

outcomes.headline: Just a talk
outcomes.text: The notes go in a drawer.

decisions.headline: Three shifts, every day
decisions.text: The Intelligence Office reports that the rival's teams work in three shifts, round the clock, every day of the week, and that the work is racing ahead because of it.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, R&D 40 % faster for two seasons at a cost in morale; if it's wrong, the morale is lost for little.

outcomes.headline: Never a quiet hour
outcomes.text: The workshop never stops, and neither does the hardware. Neither do the complaints.

outcomes.headline: Tired, not faster
outcomes.text: The rival had three shifts for a few weeks before a deadline, not as a rule. Ours are exhausted within a month and the work barely speeds up.

outcomes.headline: Our own hours
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: Read aloud, answered aloud
decisions.text: A source says the rival's test crews read every checklist aloud, and each step must be answered aloud by the person doing it before the next is read. Ours tick boxes in silence.
decisions.stakes: If the tip is right, about two seasons' gain; if it's wrong, about half a season's lost.

options.label: Try it on our test crews

outcomes.headline: Nothing skipped
outcomes.text: It feels silly for a week. Then a step is caught that everyone would have ticked without doing it, and nobody feels silly any more.

outcomes.headline: Slower and no better
outcomes.text: Without the training behind it, the crews just read faster and louder. The tests take longer and catch nothing new.

outcomes.headline: Silent ticks
outcomes.text: The report goes in a drawer.

decisions.headline: A week on the big test stand
decisions.text: The engine test centre has its largest stand free for a week. The engineers want a short campaign on the engines: firings, then the measurements that make sense of them, planned shift by shift. You can plan it yourself, or let the team run it their way.

options.label: Run it yourself
options.shows: Opens the campaign. The objective is worth about a season and a half of R&D, the bonus about three; falling short costs nothing but the chance.

outcomes.headline: A week to remember on the big stand
outcomes.text: Six firings and the measurements to match. The engines' start-up is better understood than it has ever been.

outcomes.headline: A good week on the big stand
outcomes.text: Enough firings and enough data to settle the questions the engineers came with.

outcomes.headline: Not enough on the big stand
outcomes.text: Too few firings to tell the engineers what they wanted to know. The week was not wasted, but it changed nothing.

outcomes.headline: The team's own way
outcomes.text: The team ran a quiet week of routine firings. Nothing new came of it.

decisions.headline: A week in the vacuum chamber
decisions.text: The big vacuum chamber is free for a week. The engineers want to run the craft through it as it will fly: runs in the cold and the vacuum, then the measurements that make sense of them, planned shift by shift. You can plan it yourself, or let the team run it their way.

options.label: Run it yourself
options.shows: Opens the campaign. The objective is worth about a season and a half of R&D, the bonus about three; falling short costs nothing but the chance.

outcomes.headline: A week to remember in the chamber
outcomes.text: Six runs and the measurements to match. The craft's systems are better understood than they have ever been.

outcomes.headline: A good week in the chamber
outcomes.text: Enough runs and enough data to settle the questions the engineers came with.

outcomes.headline: Not enough in the chamber
outcomes.text: Too few runs to tell the engineers what they wanted to know. The week was not wasted, but it changed nothing.

outcomes.headline: The team's own way
outcomes.text: The team ran a quiet week of routine checks in the chamber. Nothing new came of it.

decisions.headline: A week of cold-flow tests
decisions.text: Before the engine is fired again, the engineers want to pump a harmless liquid through its plumbing instead of propellant, to watch how it flows with nothing burning. Short runs are cheap; it's the measurements that are hard to come by. You can plan it yourself, or let the team run it their way.

options.label: Run it yourself
options.shows: Opens the campaign. The objective is worth about a season and a half of R&D, the bonus about three; falling short costs nothing but the chance.

outcomes.headline: A week to remember on the flow rig
outcomes.text: Run after run, filmed and measured. The engineers can now say where every drop goes, and how fast.

outcomes.headline: A good week on the flow rig
outcomes.text: Enough runs and enough readings to settle the questions the engineers came with.

outcomes.headline: Not enough on the flow rig
outcomes.text: Too few readings to make sense of the runs. The week was not wasted, but it changed nothing.

outcomes.headline: The team's own way
outcomes.text: The team ran a few routine flows and wrote them up. Nothing new came of it.

decisions.headline: A month of igniter tests
decisions.text: The igniters are the least trusted part of the engine. The engineers want a month of test ignitions, and at the end of it they must still have spare igniters good enough to fly. Every test uses one up. You can plan it yourself, or let the team run it their way.

options.label: Run it yourself
options.shows: Opens the campaign. The objective is worth about a season and a half of R&D, the bonus about three; falling short costs nothing but the chance.

outcomes.headline: Every start a clean one
outcomes.text: A month of ignitions, every one on film, and a box of spare igniters nobody doubts.

outcomes.headline: A good month of ignitions
outcomes.text: Enough clean starts to trust the design, and enough spares left to fly.

outcomes.headline: Not enough left to fly
outcomes.text: The tests used up more igniters than the team could replace. The month was not wasted, but it changed nothing.

outcomes.headline: The team's own way
outcomes.text: The team fired a handful of igniters on the bench. Nothing new came of it.

decisions.headline: A week on the shake table
decisions.text: The big shake table is free for a week. The engineers want to rattle the hardware as hard as a launch would, then measure what moved. Every full-level shake wears out the fixtures that hold it down. You can plan it yourself, or let the team run it their way.

options.label: Run it yourself
options.shows: Opens the campaign. The objective is worth about a season and a half of R&D, the bonus about three; falling short costs nothing but the chance.

outcomes.headline: A week to remember on the shake table
outcomes.text: Every frequency, every axis, and the measurements to match. Nothing on the hardware will shake loose that the team doesn't already know about.

outcomes.headline: A good week on the shake table
outcomes.text: Enough shakes and enough measurements to settle the questions the engineers came with.

outcomes.headline: Not enough on the shake table
outcomes.text: Too few shakes to tell the engineers what they wanted to know. The week was not wasted, but it changed nothing.

outcomes.headline: The team's own way
outcomes.text: The team ran the standard shake and nothing more. Nothing new came of it.

decisions.headline: A week under the sun lamps
decisions.text: The sun simulator, a chamber with banks of lamps as bright as sunlight in space, is free for a week. The engineers want to roast the craft, map its hot spots and fit new insulating blankets, all in one campaign. You can plan it yourself, or let the team run it their way.

options.label: Run it yourself
options.shows: Opens the campaign. The objective is worth about a season and a half of R&D, the bonus about three; falling short costs nothing but the chance.

outcomes.headline: A week to remember under the lamps
outcomes.text: Every hot spot mapped and every blanket refitted. The craft will keep its temperature in sun and shadow alike.

outcomes.headline: A good week under the lamps
outcomes.text: Enough runs, measurements and new blankets to settle the questions the engineers came with.

outcomes.headline: Not enough under the lamps
outcomes.text: The week ran out before the campaign came together. It was not wasted, but it changed nothing.

outcomes.headline: The team's own way
outcomes.text: The team ran the craft under the lamps for a day and wrote up the temperatures. Nothing new came of it.

decisions.headline: All the systems at once
decisions.text: The craft's systems have each passed their own tests. Now the engineers want a week of switching them on together, in flight order, logging every channel and swapping out any box that misbehaves. You can plan it yourself, or let the team run it their way.

options.label: Run it yourself
options.shows: Opens the campaign. The objective is worth about a season and a half of R&D, the bonus about three; falling short costs nothing but the chance.

outcomes.headline: A week to remember on the test floor
outcomes.text: Test after test, every channel logged and every bad box swapped. The craft behaves as one machine.

outcomes.headline: A good week on the test floor
outcomes.text: Enough tests and enough logs to settle the questions the engineers came with.

outcomes.headline: Not enough on the test floor
outcomes.text: Too few tests to tell the engineers what they wanted to know. The week was not wasted, but it changed nothing.

outcomes.headline: The team's own way
outcomes.text: The team switched everything on once and watched the lights. Nothing new came of it.
